facts.statement: Avalonnectes is an extinct genus of small rhomaleosaurid plesiosaur known from the Early Jurassic period in the United Kingdom.
facts.quote: Avalonnectes is an extinct genus of small-bodied rhomaleosaurid known from the Early Jurassic period (most likely earliest Hettangian stage) of the United Kingdom.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen NHMUK 14550 includes the back of a skull and a nearly complete, articulated postcranial skeleton preserved in three dimensions.
facts.quote: Avalonnectes is known from the holotype specimen NHMUK 14550, which consists of the posterior portion of a skull, and a nearly complete, three-dimensionally preserved and articulated postcranial skeleton.

facts.statement: Fossils of Avalonnectes were collected at Street in Somerset from the Pre-Planorbis beds of the Blue Lias Formation.
facts.quote: Both specimens were collected at Street, of Somerset, from the Pre-Planorbis beds of the Blue Lias Formation of the Lower Lias Group.

facts.statement: Avalonnectes lived approximately 199.6 to 198 million years ago during the earliest Hettangian stage, just after the Triassic-Jurassic boundary.
facts.quote: Thus, they probably fall within the earliest Hettangian P. tilmanni Chronozone, which is about 199.6-198 million years old, immediately following the Triassic–Jurassic Boundary.

facts.statement: Avalonnectes is considered one of the oldest known plesiosaurs because its fossils represent the earliest occurrence of the group.
facts.quote: Plesiosaurs fossils which were discovered at Street represent the earliest known occurrence of the Plesiosauria. Hence, Avalonnectes is one of the oldest plesiosaurs to date.

facts.statement: Avalonnectes possessed only 18 to 19 dorsal vertebrae, a low number that serves as a unique distinguishing feature.
facts.quote: The number of dorsal vertebrae are about 18–19; this low number represents its autapomorphy.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis suggests Avalonnectes is a basal member of the rhomaleosaurid family.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis performed by Benson et al. (2012) found it to be a basal rhomaleosaurid.

facts.statement: The genus Avalonnectes was named by Benson, Evans, and Druckenmiller in 2012, with Avalonnectes arturi as the type species.
facts.quote: Avalonnectes was first described and named by Roger B. J. Benson, Mark Evans and Patrick S. Druckenmiller in 2012 and the type species is Avalonnectes arturi.

facts.statement: The name Avalonnectes combines 'Avalon', an island from King Arthur legends near the discovery site, with the Greek word for 'swimmer'.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Avalon, an island from the legend of King Arthur, often identified with Glastonbury, near Street, and from Greek nectes, meaning "swimmer".

facts.statement: The species name 'arturi' honors paleontologist Arthur Cruickshank, who began restudying British Lower Jurassic plesiosaurs in the 1990s.
facts.quote: The specific name honors the paleontologist Arthur Cruickshank (1932–2011), who with M. A. Taylor initiated the restudy of British Lower Jurassic plesiosaurians in the 1990s.

facts.statement: The fossil record for Avalonnectes spans from 201.4 to 199.5 million years ago during the Hettangian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Hettangian (201.4 to 199.5 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Avalonnectes had a body length of 73.5 cm and a neck length exceeding 67 cm.
rejected.quote: Avalonnectes is a small-bodied rhomaleosaurid, with a trunck length of 73.5 cm and a neck length of more than 67 cm.
